newsitem.title: USA: US debt allocations mostly steady Oct 22 wk - survey.
newsitem.headline: US debt allocations mostly steady Oct 22 wk - survey.

text.p: Money managers once again made offsetting adjustments to their U.S. debt allocations in the past week, leaving portfolios largely unchanged, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.

"As has been the case in recent weeks, there were flows in both directions," the report said. "There does not appear to be widespread market conviction that the complexion of the bond market is going to change."

In the week ended October 22, the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading was unchanged at 4.44, while the asset-weighted number climbed to 4.73, up from 4.33 in the previous period, according the report.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio rose to 7.00 percent from 6.98 percent.
Duration bogey held mostly rose to 4.12 on an arithmetic basis and 4.66 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

Twelve percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from 24 percent the week before. The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active was 4.33, down from 4.83 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
